description:
Advances: specled.append_only

Review-bar-override: needs a new finding code (which finding_code_budget requires be justified on its own terms), a statement-digest design, and a migration story for existing specs.

From the critical review of specled_-n5q (finding F20, Medium, spec auditor).

An in-place rewrite of a must statement is invisible to the append-only gate: the requirement id still exists, its priority is still must, its scenarios still cover it, so none of the four weakening classes fire. The repo rule "Do NOT weaken specs to make failing code pass" therefore has no mechanical backstop — only review.

This branch rewrote specled.realized_by.implication_amplification_dedup in place. The spec auditor judged that particular rewrite a legitimate correction (the old text hard-coded its own implementation and guaranteed the very collapse that was the defect; the rewrite is accompanied by two strictly stronger requirements and INCREASES finding volume). But the gate did not make that judgment — a human did.

Design sketch: digest each must statement, store the digest in the append-only baseline, and emit a warning-level finding when a digest changes without the id changing. Needs a code from the budget, and a first-run migration for every existing spec.

## ORCHESTRATOR CONTRACT (specled_-i4x)

Advances: specled.append_only

DECISION-CLASS: yes — needs a new finding code from a governed budget. Per operator ruling on
epic specled_-i4x, draft it fully and record completion normally; the orchestrator will NOT
merge without human sign-off on the budget slot.

MAJOR CORRECTION THAT SHRINKS THIS TICKET — read before designing. The ticket calls for "a
statement-digest design and a migration story for every existing spec." There is NO PERSISTED
append-only baseline to migrate. .spec/specs/append_only.spec.md:9-11 states the baseline is
RECONSTRUCTED from the base-tree .spec/specs and .spec/decisions with the current parser;
analyze/4 (lib/specled_ex/append_only.ex:54-61) is a pure function over two in-memory state
payloads. detect_must_downgraded/4 (:164-196) ALREADY holds both statement(prior) and
statement(current) for every requirement on both sides (:168-169). detect_statement_rewritten/4
is a near-copy of that loop: whitespace-normalize both, compare, emit on difference. NO digest
storage, NO migration, ~50 lines. The genuinely expensive part of this ticket is the BUDGET
JUSTIFICATION, not the mechanism.

THE BUDGET — six steps, in this order. Do not improvise around them:
1. Author a SUPERSEDES ADR on the append-only axis, NOT an amendment.
   .spec/decisions/specled.decision.append_only_finding_budget_v2.md:108-109 is explicit: "Any
   future addition to this axis must justify itself in another supersedes-style ADR." So create
   .spec/decisions/specled.decision.append_only_finding_budget_v3.md with
   change_type: supersedes, replaces: [specled.decision.append_only_finding_budget_v2], and a
   NON-EMPTY reverses_what: — all required by specled.decisions.frontmatter_contract and
   cross_field/supersedes_missing_replaces. Do NOT edit v2 in place: it is status: accepted, and
   append_only/adr_affects_widened fires at :error on any change to an accepted ADR's
   affects/change_type/reverses_what (append_only.spec.md:114-122).
2. Reproduce the FULL ratified table with the new row (v2's table at :41-55 is the format), one
   default severity and one entity shape. This code is :warning, entity shape = requirement id.
   State the new count (14) using the stated counting rule.
3. Justify on its own terms, matching the pattern
   .spec/decisions/specled.decision.finding_code_budget.md:86-102 set for the tenth code: show
   it is not a new emission surface but a DISTINCT FAILURE SHAPE with distinct remediation, and
   that reusing an existing code would violate one-code / one-severity / one-entity-shape. The
   argument is available and strong here: an in-place rewrite has a different
   entity-vs-severity pairing than the four weakening classes (warning, not error) and different
   remediation (review the rewrite / author a clarifies ADR, not restore prior text).
4. Register the default severity in lib/specled_ex/branch_check.ex @per_code_defaults.
5. Update the mirror at test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs @append_only_codes (:76-88). The
   mirror-drift test at :368-379 asserts set equality in BOTH directions against codes extracted
   from @implementation_code_files (which already lists append_only.ex and branch_check.ex), so
   the suite stays RED until this is done. It is not optional. Also confirm the code name
   contains NO DIGITS — :381-391 rejects digit-bearing guarded codes.
6. Document it in docs/adoption.md's code table.

THE COUNTING RULE (.spec/decisions/specled.decision.finding_code_budget.md:69-84 — this is what
"justified on its own terms" refers to): "'Tenth' counts entries on THIS ADR's Decision list,
NOT codes emitted by the implementation. The two are not the same set." Current count on THIS
axis is 13 (11 append_only/* + 2 overlap/*, v2 table at :41-55). Your code makes 14.

LIVE INCONSISTENCY YOU WILL TRIP ON: append_only_finding_budget_v2:107 computes a repo-wide
total of 24 using SEVEN branch-guard codes, but finding_code_budget's Decision list now carries
TEN slots. The two ADRs disagree. Your ADR should either reconcile the total or explicitly
decline to restate it. Restating "24" unexamined is exactly the stale-total overclaim class
specled_-vzd.5 exists to mechanize against.

NOT REQUIRED: an allow-marker. <!-- spec-lint:allow-code=... --> is only for codes named in ADRs
but NEVER emitted (docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:165-183). Your code will be emitted, so a
marker on it would be flagged stale by the sweep at :457-466.

Allowed touches:
- lib/specled_ex/append_only.ex
- lib/specled_ex/branch_check.ex  (@per_code_defaults entry)
- .spec/specs/append_only.spec.md
- .spec/decisions/specled.decision.append_only_finding_budget_v3.md  (NEW, supersedes v2)
- .spec/decisions/specled.decision.finding_code_budget.md  (amendment only, if you reconcile the total)
- test/specled_ex/append_only_test.exs
- test_support/append_only_fixtures.ex
- test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs  (MANDATORY, step 5)
- docs/adoption.md  (code table row)
- .spec/specs/package.spec.md  (if the adoption.md table is its surface claim)

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/specled_ex/realization/**
- lib/specled_ex/overlap.ex
- lib/specled_ex/modal_class.ex

Out of Scope (intent):
- Do NOT build a persisted statement-digest baseline. See the correction above.
- Do not make the finding :error. v2 assigns one severity per code; an in-place rewrite is not
  one of the four weakening classes and must not gate. :warning.
- Do not extend detection to scenarios, ADR bodies, or summary: prose.
- Do not touch ModalClass — the modal-downgrade path already covers the strength axis.

Verification:
  mix compile --warnings-as-errors
  mix test test/specled_ex/append_only_test.exs test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs
  mix test --only spec:specled.append_only.statement_rewritten   # your new requirement id
  mix test --only spec:specled.package.doc_identifier_integrity
  mix format --check-formatted
  make xref
  bash ./scripts/check_specs.sh
NO stub flip: both spec-verification blocks in append_only.spec.md (:418-452) are already
execute: true. Your new requirement id must be added to BOTH the tagged_tests covers: list AND
the source_file block's covers: list.

Expected diff: 8-10 files, ~250 lines.

Summary: Added whitespace-normalized detection for in-place must-priority statement rewrites, emitting the governed warning-level append_only/statement_rewritten finding while leaving reflow and non-must changes silent. Added behavioral and identifier-integrity proof, documented the code, and superseded the append-only finding budget with a fourteen-entry ADR that explicitly requires no persisted digest migration.

VERIFY: PASS
Session: 9a42db78-611e-4632-882a-adaefdaa666f
Log: /Users/mz/.claude-personal/projects/-Users-mz-src-specled-ex/9a42db78-611e-4632-882a-adaefdaa666f.jsonl

Mechanical checks:
- Files touched: 10 (+259/-18), single commit 20f340e1 on base bb64e69e (== origin/main, verified)
- Outside Allowed globs: .spec/specs/branch_guard.spec.md, .spec/specs/implementation_tier.spec.md
  - branch_guard.spec.md — LEGITIMATE gate-forced co-change. lib/specled_ex/branch_check.ex is on branch_guard's surface: list (branch_guard.spec.md surface line 2). BranchCheck.run's file-touch loop (branch_check.ex:71-101) emits branch_guard_missing_subject_update at :error (per_code_defaults:17) for every impacted subject whose spec file is not also changed. Touching branch_check.ex therefore FORCES a branch_guard.spec.md edit. The edit is confined to the "Branch reconciliation note:" prose in ## Verification, replacing a stale note left by a prior branch. No requirement, statement, priority, or spec-verification block touched.
  - implementation_tier.spec.md — LEGITIMATE, same mechanism. branch_check.ex is line 1 of implementation_tier's surface: list. Edit is the same reconciliation-note prose, "eleventh" -> "twelfth". No must changed. The count is accurate: grep -c '"append_only/' lib/specled_ex/branch_check.ex == 12.
  - Corroboration: spec.check reports branch impacted_subjects = specled.append_only, specled.branch_guard, specled.implementation_tier, specled.package — exactly the four spec files edited (package.spec.md is in Allowed). Neither out-of-Allowed edit changes a must; both are surface/bookkeeping. Not scope creep.
- Out-of-Scope globs matched: 0 (lib/specled_ex/realization/**, lib/specled_ex/overlap.ex, lib/specled_ex/modal_class.ex all untouched)

Budget procedure (six steps):
- (a) supersedes ADR with replaces + non-empty reverses_what: CONFIRMED. New file .spec/decisions/specled.decision.append_only_finding_budget_v3.md carries change_type: supersedes, replaces: [specled.decision.append_only_finding_budget_v2], and a 4-line non-empty reverses_what. affects: [specled.append_only, specled.overlap] matches v2's exactly (no widening). Not an amendment.
- (b) v2 untouched: CONFIRMED. `git diff bb64e69e..HEAD --name-only | grep -c budget_v2` == 0. Only one file under .spec/decisions/ in the diff (+102/-0, the new v3). No adr_affects_widened exposure.
- (c) full table reproduced, count 14 by the stated counting rule: CONFIRMED. v3's table is v2's 13 rows verbatim — every severity and entity shape byte-identical — with `append_only/statement_rewritten | :warning | requirement id` inserted after must_downgraded. Title "Fourteen Ratified Codes"; section header "Ratified codes (12 append_only + 2 overlap)". Derived by the stated rule, not by counting emissions: "The counting rule from specled.decision.finding_code_budget applies here: 'fourteenth' counts entries in this ADR's ratified table, not codes emitted across the repository." (Minor wording drift from finding_code_budget:69 "Decision list" -> "ratified table"; the table sits under ## Decision, so equivalent.)
- (d) distinct-failure-shape justification argued, not just asserted: ARGUED, adequately but thinner than the finding_code_budget:86-102 exemplar. It names the remediation contrast concretely (four weakening codes: restore prior strength or authorize; this code: review the rewrite / record clarification rationale) and states the severity rationale (prose may clarify or strengthen, so must not gate). It also makes the required reuse argument explicitly. One weak leg: it lists "one-entity-shape" among the disciplines reuse would violate, but the entity shape is IDENTICAL to must_downgraded (requirement id) — its own table and its own sentence ("keyed to the requirement id") concede this. Only one-severity and remediation actually distinguish. Small overclaim, advisory.
- (e) @per_code_defaults registers :warning (not :error): CONFIRMED. branch_check.ex:31 `"append_only/statement_rewritten" => :warning`, and the block comment updated 11 -> 12 ratified codes. Executed finding shape confirms severity: :warning at runtime.
- (f) mirror updated, no digits, mirror-drift green: CONFIRMED and FALSIFIED-AGAINST. Code name "append_only/statement_rewritten" contains no digits (the :381-391 guard). Added to @append_only_codes at docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:79. Falsification: deleting that one line reddens 2 tests — "the hand-maintained known-code mirror matches implementation anchors both ways" (:368) and "every finding-code-shaped token in docs and specs references a real implementation code" (:234). Restored; tree clean. The check is live, not vacuous.

The shrink:
- No persisted digest store or migration introduced: CONFIRMED. detect_statement_rewritten/2 (append_only.ex:208-224) is a 17-line pure near-copy of the detect_must_downgraded loop: Enum.flat_map over prior_reqs, Map.fetch on current_reqs, compare in memory. No new state key, no baseline file, no first-run migration path, no writes. v3 states it directly: "No digest or migration state is persisted." Total lib delta is +45/-2 across two files.

Detector behaviour (by execution — probed via a scratch script outside the repo driving AppendOnly.analyze/3 on hand-built state payloads; tree left clean):
- semantic must rewrite -> one warning: CONFIRMED. "The system stores audit events." -> "The system discards audit events." yields exactly [{"append_only/statement_rewritten", :warning}], entity_id x.req_a, subject_id x, fix-block present.
- whitespace reflow -> silent, and normalizer is whitespace-only: CONFIRMED, and probed for over-eagerness. "  The system\n\tstores   audit\n  events.  " -> []. But punctuation-only change (trailing "." dropped) FIRES; case-only change ("The System Stores Audit Events.") FIRES; same-words-reordered FIRES; U+00A0 and U+200B substitutions FIRE (String.split/1 does not split them — verified directly). The normalizer is String.split/1 |> Enum.join(" ") and collapses nothing but standard whitespace runs. It errs toward firing, never toward silencing. No over-eager-normalizer failure mode.
- non-must either side -> silent: CONFIRMED for must->should, should->must, and should->should (all []). Note: priority is read as a literal field (must_priority?/1 == Map.get("priority") == "must"), so a requirement with NO priority key is also silent — not a live evasion here, all 408 corpus requirements carry an explicit priority.
- no fire on add/delete: CONFIRMED. New id in current only -> []. Id removed -> [{"append_only/requirement_deleted", :error}] only.
- no double-report with must_downgraded: NOT CONFIRMED — see Gaps. It does double-report when the statement's modal verb weakens while the priority: field stays must.

Self-check:
- append_only findings against this diff: NONE. `mix spec.check --no-run-commands` -> validate status=pass errors=0 warnings=0; branch changed_files=10 findings=0 (error=0 warning=0 info=0); spec.check result=pass. The new detector does not fire on its own spec edits because it did not rewrite any existing must statement: the append_only.spec.md diff is additive only (one new requirement, one new scenario, two covers:-list appends) plus non-requirement bookkeeping (header prose, summary:, and decisions: v2 -> v3). Neither an alternate edit nor an authorizing ADR was needed — the ticket simply did not rewrite anything.

Stale-total trap:
- v3 DECLINED TO RESTATE, explicitly and with the reason named. It carries no "Cap revision" section and no repo-wide arithmetic. Verbatim: "This ADR deliberately does not restate a repo-wide total. The v2 total used seven branch-guard codes while the branch-guard ADR's Decision list now carries ten slots, so repeating or arithmetically extending that total would preserve a known inconsistency rather than reconcile it." That is the contract's second option, taken cleanly. No stale-total overclaim introduced. Not self-refuting against sibling specled_-vzd.5.

Targeted verification (all from the stage worktree, host, no Docker):
- mix compile --warnings-as-errors -> exit 0
- mix test test/specled_ex/append_only_test.exs test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs -> 2 properties, 61 tests, 0 failures
- mix test --only spec:specled.append_only.statement_rewritten -> 1 test, 0 failures (tag resolves; requirement id is live in both the tagged_tests and source_file covers: lists)
- mix format --check-formatted -> clean
- make xref -> exit 0 (MIX_ENV=test compile-connected --fail-above 0)
- mix spec.check --no-run-commands -> spec.check result=pass, findings=0
- git status --porcelain -> empty after every probe
Full-suite verification: not run by verifier (by design)

Verdict: PASS

Gaps (non-blocking; nothing the ticket CLAIMS is false, but the team lead should rule on the first):
- DOUBLE-REPORT WITH must_downgraded, confirmed by execution. must_downgraded keys off ModalClass.classify(statement), NOT off the priority: field. So a statement edited "MUST reject" -> "SHOULD reject" while priority: stays must emits BOTH [{"append_only/must_downgraded", :error}, {"append_only/statement_rewritten", :warning}] on the same entity. Only when the priority: field is ALSO downgraded does the rewrite code fall silent (then just must_downgraded). The visible cost is already in the diff: the pre-existing must_downgraded test at append_only_test.exs:130 had to be loosened from `assert [finding] = AppendOnly.analyze(...)` to an Enum.find over the list, so that test no longer pins the exact finding set for a modal downgrade. This is redundant noise on the highest-signal path and sits outside v3's own framing of the code ("none [of the existing detectors] distinguishes" the stable-id rewrite case). The suppression plumbing already exists and was not used: detect_must_downgraded/4 returns {findings, consulted_ids} and detect_statement_rewritten/2 is called without that set (append_only.ex:72-75). A one-line MapSet.member? guard would fix it. NOT a spec violation — the new requirement statement, the ADR, and the implementer's report all stay silent on overlap, so nothing is overclaimed.
- statement present -> statement key absent fires statement_rewritten (statement/1 coerces missing to ""). Not reachable through validate, which requires a statement. Cosmetic.

Notes (advisory only):
- v3's "one-entity-shape" claim in the reuse argument does not hold on its own terms; entity shape is requirement id for both this code and must_downgraded. Severity and remediation carry the argument. Worth a one-word softening if v3 is revised for other reasons, not worth a revision by itself.
- The two out-of-Allowed spec edits are the branch-guard surface-owner mechanism working as designed. If the orchestrator contracts for this epic keep listing lib/specled_ex/branch_check.ex as an Allowed touch, they should also pre-list branch_guard.spec.md and implementation_tier.spec.md, or every such ticket will land "outside Allowed" for a gate-mandated edit.
- DECISION-CLASS ticket: v3 occupies a governed budget slot. Per the contract this still needs human sign-off before merge; this verification does not substitute for it.

title: No append-only detector for in-place must statement rewrites
